not_covered: The United States moved to force the sale or ban of TikTok due to national-security concerns regarding potential Chinese government access to US user data and its algorithm, as determined through CFIUS review [Source: ev-1].

This legal pressure was formalized when President Biden signed the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act on 2024-04-24, which mandated that ByteDance divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90) or face a US ban [Source: ev-1].

This arrangement placed US user data in Oracle's cloud under US control, granted Oracle about a 12.5% stake alongside SoftBank and other investors, while allowing ByteDance to retain a majority interest; Vice President JD Vance led the White House negotiations for this structure, with final ownership completed through 2025 [Source: ev-1].
